wave: REPRESENT-VQ-1: a representation that depends on another represented object
frozen: 2026-09-06, before any implementation, against the VERIFIED merge commit of PROGRESSIVE-1: main `f5a50e27` (merge of PR #440), with the wave's own commit `624aa59f` confirmed as an ancestor. Branch `represent-vq-1`, worktree `.claude/worktrees/represent-vq-1`. The two corrections, two tightenings, two guardrails and the certificate-vocabulary preference below were all folded in BEFORE this freeze on the user's review of the draft; nothing here is a later edit, and any contract movement from now on is recorded as a FINDING rather than designed away.
lane: Semantic/plugin lane. The performance lane stays PAUSED: nothing here is measured in seconds, and no claim in this wave is about speed.
why: `AuxiliaryOperands` has been in the contract since it was written — a named map of `OperandRef` on `CodecOperands`, empty for every codec, put there so that 'a codebook arrives as a dependency and not as a stream'. Nothing has ever put one there, so the claim is untested. PROGRESSIVE-1 settled the extent axis; this settles the dependency axis. They are the two hostile cases the representation plane must survive before `RepresentationCodec` v1 can be frozen, and the question is exactly one: can one representation depend on another REPRESENTED OBJECT while selection, validation, accounting, provider identity and canonical execution stay generic?

reconnaissance_2026_09_06.V1: `AuxiliaryOperands` (`represent/codec/streams.rs`) is a `BTreeMap<String, OperandRef>` on `CodecOperands`, built empty by `from_streams` and empty in every codec — the only thing any test asserts about it is that it IS empty. No trait method declares what a codec REQUIRES, so nothing can check a dependency before bytes are read.
reconnaissance_2026_09_06.V2: The loader resolves ONE operand at a time: `OperandStore::load_at` → `load_raw(object, tensor)` → decode. Nothing recurses, so today no cycle can exist and no closure is computed. Recursion, ordering and cycle refusal are all new.
reconnaissance_2026_09_06.V3: **The container has nowhere to record a reference.** `SegmentTensor { name, dtype, shape, offset, len }` (serde, `SEGMENT_HEADER_SCHEMA = 1`) carries no metadata; the graph's `Representation { encoding, fidelity }` carries none; the precision map is a compilation POLICY, not a per-operand table. And a shared codebook cannot ride PROGRESSIVE-1's sibling-name convention (`<tensor>.<stream>`), because a sibling belongs to one tensor and the point of this wave is that two operands share one object.
reconnaissance_2026_09_06.V4: Provider invalidation exists — `PreparedOperands::ensure_providers_in(registry)` (rung 3d), witnessed in `tests/external_codec_provider.rs`. A codebook stored under its own codec must participate: losing the CODEBOOK's provider must invalidate the image, not only losing the codes' provider.
reconnaissance_2026_09_06.V5: `ResourceLedger::aggregate` already sums `stored`, `mapped` and `read_to_prepare` ONCE per distinct (object, tensor), so a shared codebook's stored footprint counts once for free. Everything else about a dependency's cost is unrepresented: `resident` and `touch_per_token` are summed per operation from the pinned realization's declared profile, and no realization has ever declared anything about an operand it merely READ.
reconnaissance_2026_09_06.V6: The planner's closure pass gives a sibling stream a fate (`build.rs::auxiliary_stream_of`, PROGRESSIVE-1), but a codebook tensor is not a sibling by name. It will report as an `UnclassifiedOperand` until the closure learns that a REFERENCED operand has a fate — the same shape of blocker PROGRESSIVE-1 hit, which is why it is predicted here rather than discovered.
reconnaissance_2026_09_06.V7: `F32_PLANES` has streams stored apart but NO auxiliary dependency, so it cannot on its own exercise transitive resolution: a codebook stored as planes is still a one-level closure. Anything claiming topological ordering needs a dependency that itself has one.

design.codec: `VQ8_SHARED` (family `VQ8_SHARED`, revision 1): one `u8` code per VECTOR of four elements, decoded through a codebook of 256 vectors. Deliberately the simplest scheme in which grouping is real — a code is not an element, so a row's codes and its values have different lengths and nothing can accidentally treat the codebook as a scale.
design.streams: `codes` (`StreamRole::Values`), local, `k/4` bytes per row. Nothing else is local: the codebook is NOT a stream.
design.auxiliaries: `codebook` — declared by the codec as REQUIRED, resolved to an `OperandRef`, loaded through the same machinery as any other operand: its own codec, its own extent, its own provider, its own realization. The codec asks for values; it does not know how the codebook is stored.

reference_table.user_correction: Persist references as an optional VERSIONED table keyed by `(owner OperandRef, auxiliary name) → target OperandRef`, never by tensor-name convention.
reference_table.shape: A container-level table with its own schema version, absent from every container written before this wave, so nothing existing changes meaning. Keyed by the OWNER operand and the auxiliary NAME the codec declared — which is what makes a shared target expressible (two owners, one target) and a name collision impossible. Never derived from a tensor's spelling: PROGRESSIVE-1's sibling rule is a NAME convention for streams of one tensor, and a dependency is a reference between operands.
reference_table.why_not_segment_tensor: A per-tensor field in the segment header can only address tensors of that segment and would re-introduce naming as identity. A cross-object reference is the normal case for a shared codebook.

arms: Arm 1 — raw f32 codebook: isolates auxiliary RESOLUTION (closure, ordering, refusals, accounting) with a dependency whose own representation is trivial.

Arm 2 — `F32_PLANES` codebook: the dependency itself has a representation, extents, a provider and a realization, so a codebook extent becomes a selectable fidelity of the thing that decodes another thing — and the parent's fidelity must COMPOSE with it (see the composed certificate below).

Arm 3 (transitive, synthetic) — a codebook that ITSELF declares an auxiliary, built in tests only, so topological order has two levels to order. Without it, nothing in the shipped codecs can exercise transitivity (V7).
design.sharing: Two weight operands reference ONE codebook, so every accounting question is asked in its sharp form.

accounting_is_realization_scoped.user_correction: Auxiliary identity does not determine residency or touch; the SELECTED REALIZATION does.
under_canonical_decode: stored footprint: once, per distinct stored object — a container fact, independent of any realization.

preparation reads: whatever ACTUALLY occurs — once if the dependency is resolved once for both owners, twice if it is scanned twice. The witness reads the store's counter and the ledger must agree with it, not with an assumption about sharing.
persistent residency: ZERO, unless the chosen realization retains the codebook. Canonical decode does not: once the weights are f32, the codebook is finished with.
per-token touch: ZERO for the same reason — the executor streams the decoded f32 image, not the codes and not the codebook.
accounting_is_realization_scoped.under_a_hypothetical_direct_vq_realizati: It would declare PERSISTENT codebook residency and PER-TOKEN codebook touch, because it reads codes and the codebook at execution time. No such realization is built in VQ-1; what VQ-1 must prove is that the accounting is EXPRESSED so that it could, i.e. the numbers come from the realization's declaration rather than from the operand being an auxiliary.
accounting_is_realization_scoped.consequence: The naive reading — 'a shared codebook is resident once and touched once per use' — is wrong twice over under canonical decode, and would bake a direct-kernel assumption into a wave that has no kernel. W4 and W5 are stated in the corrected form.
accounting_is_realization_scoped.guardrail_control_is_not_a_candidate: **The retained-codebook control never enters the selectable candidate set.** It exists to prove the accounting reads a realization's declaration rather than an operand's role, and it is exercised at the PRICING/PROFILE layer only — a declared profile handed to the ledger, never a realization the backend offers as a candidate. A declaration with no implementation must never be pinnable: the planner selects only physically executable realizations, and a control that could be selected would break exactly the invariant the rest of this contract rests on.

composed_fidelity.user_correction: A shallow `F32_PLANES` codebook changes the fidelity of the parent VQ representation. Two independent certificates are not enough: the planner needs a COMPOSED certificate, `r(decoded VQ) <= r(VQ assignment) + r(codebook extent)` in the codec's declared norm and domain, and a parent quality floor must be evaluated against it.
composed_fidelity.shape: The parent codec composes: given its own extent and the certificates of its resolved auxiliaries, it states the certificate a caller may rely on. That is expected to be a SECOND trait addition beside `required_auxiliaries` — an honest contract finding, not a failure, and pre-registered here so it cannot be reported as a surprise.
composed_fidelity.consequence_for_selection: A parent floor may force a DEEPER auxiliary extent, or refuse when no combination satisfies it. Selecting the codebook's extent purely by what the codebook alone certifies would silently degrade every operand that depends on it.
composed_fidelity.consequence_for_conformance: `codec::conformance` measures the parent's decoded error against the SOURCE at (parent extent, auxiliary extent) pairs and holds it against the composed bound — the same discipline PROGRESSIVE-1 applied to a single certificate, applied to a composition.
composed_fidelity.guardrail_norms_and_domains: **Composition refuses what it cannot compose.** A certificate today carries a bare number (`ErrorRadius { relative_rms }`) and its norm and domain live in prose — relative RMS over finite normals, by PROGRESSIVE-1's convention. Composition makes that implicitness dangerous: adding an auxiliary's max-absolute bound to a parent's L2 bound would manufacture a guarantee nobody made. So the certificate must NAME its norm and its certified domain, and composition must REFUSE by name when an auxiliary's norm or domain is not the one the parent composes in — never silently convert, never widen, never take the number and drop the units. That is expected to be a THIRD contract addition (a norm and domain on `ErrorRadius`), pre-registered here with the other two, and a refusal witness goes with it: an auxiliary certified in a different norm makes the parent's composed certificate UNAVAILABLE rather than optimistic.

design.boundary: No direct kernel, no codebook caching, no AQLM, no optimiser change, no new selection algorithm. Each would confound the question. And no `AuxiliaryOperands` special case: if the loader, the planner or the accounting says the word 'codebook', the wave has failed its own test.

certificate_vocabulary.user_preference: Do not expose another externally constructible public-field struct before v1 is frozen. The certificate gets validated constructors and accessors — `FidelityCertificate::new(metric_id, domain_id, radius)?` — so future metadata can be added without breaking providers.
certificate_vocabulary.semantic_ids_not_enums: The metric and the domain are VERSIONED SEMANTIC IDS, not closed enums. A closed enum would limit the supposedly open plugin plane to the metrics LARQL happens to ship: a provider that certifies in a metric this build never heard of must be able to SAY so, and be refused for incompatibility rather than for being unspellable.
certificate_vocabulary.vq1_scope: VQ-1 requires EXACT metric and domain identity for composition — same metric id, same domain id, or the composed certificate is unavailable by name. Domain-SUBSET reasoning is deliberately future work: it is a lattice question, and getting it wrong would silently widen a guarantee, which is the exact failure the guardrail exists to prevent.
certificate_vocabulary.consequence_for_progressive: `F32_PLANES`'s existing radius becomes a `FidelityCertificate` carrying the metric it always meant (relative RMS) over the domain it always meant (finite normals), stated rather than implied. PROGRESSIVE-1's out-of-tree provider constructs one through the validated constructor, which is the point of introducing it before the freeze rather than after.

witnesses.W1_closure_before_bytes: The complete auxiliary closure — transitively — is admitted at preparation BEFORE any payload read, witnessed on the store's own read counter: metadata only, no payload.
witnesses.W2_refusals_by_name: A missing reference, an incompatible codebook shape, a missing provider for the AUXILIARY's codec, a self-reference, and a dependency cycle are each refused by name, before I/O, naming the owner, the auxiliary name and the target.
witnesses.W3_topological: Dependencies resolve deepest-first, asserted on the synthetic two-level arm (V7: the shipped codecs cannot exercise this alone). Order is asserted, not incidental.
witnesses.W4_footprint_once: The shared codebook's STORED footprint counts once across its two owners — a container fact, asserted under both arms.
witnesses.W5_realization_decides_lifetime: Under canonical decode the codebook's PERSISTENT RESIDENCY and PER-TOKEN TOUCH are ZERO, and its PREPARATION READS are what the store's counter actually recorded. Beside it, a declaration-level control: a realization profile that RETAINS the codebook prices it as persistent residency and per-token touch, proving the numbers come from the realization and not from the operand's role. The control is priced, never selected — it is not in any candidate set, and a test asserts that the backend never offers it, so no declaration without an implementation can be pinned.
witnesses.W6_composed_certificate: The parent's certificate at (parent extent, codebook extent) is the composed bound, the measured parent error respects it, and a parent floor is evaluated against the COMPOSED certificate — forcing a deeper codebook extent where a shallow one would break the floor, and refusing when no combination satisfies it. And the refusal arm: an auxiliary whose certificate is stated in a different norm or over a different domain makes the composed certificate unavailable, by name, rather than being converted into the parent's units.
witnesses.W7_invalidation: Removing the codebook's provider invalidates a prepared image through `ensure_providers_in`, naming the auxiliary's label — not only the codes' label.
witnesses.W8_out_of_tree: An external crate's codec consumes an auxiliary operand and executes, with no shipped label appearing anywhere in execution code.
witnesses.W9_no_hidden_pathway: Nothing in the loader, planner or accounting branches on 'codebook' or on `VQ8_SHARED`: the external provider's auxiliary is named something else entirely, and that is what proves the path is generic.

implementation_order: 3. Metadata-only closure admission and DAG refusal before I/O.
5. The progressive-codebook arm with composed fidelity.

predictions.Q1: `RepresentationCodec` and its vocabulary need ADDITIONS ONLY — a declaration of required auxiliaries, a composed-certificate method, and a validated `FidelityCertificate` (metric id, domain id, radius) replacing the bare `ErrorRadius` number — with no change to any existing method's parameters or return type beyond the certificate type itself. FALSIFIED if `decode_rows` or `validate` must change shape to carry a resolved dependency, which would mean `CodecOperands` was the wrong seam. Note on scoring: providers that construct a certificate must move to the validated constructor — PROGRESSIVE-1's out-of-tree test included. That is the vocabulary extension this wave exists to settle before v1 is frozen, and it is not a falsification.
predictions.Q2: The container needs exactly one new declared thing — the versioned reference table — and no change to how any existing container reads. FALSIFIED if the graph or the precision map must also learn about dependencies.
predictions.Q3: The closure pass needs the same TREATMENT as PROGRESSIVE-1's siblings — a referenced operand has a fate — and no role vocabulary change. FALSIFIED if a codebook needs an `OperandRole`, which would make a dependency a model concept rather than a representation one.
predictions.Q4: Accounting needs no new resource DIMENSION: footprint already dedupes per object, preparation reads are already counted per object, and residency and touch already come from the pinned realization's declaration. What it needs is for a dependency's reads to be attributed at all. FALSIFIED if a dependency needs a dimension of its own the way an extent needed `read_to_prepare`.
predictions.Q5: Arm 2 works with no VQ-specific code: a codebook stored as `F32_PLANES` is loaded by the same path that loads any operand, extent selection included. FALSIFIED if the auxiliary loader must special-case a progressive dependency.
predictions.Q6: An external provider can do all of it through exported API alone, as PROGRESSIVE-1's did. FALSIFIED if any auxiliary handling requires a match arm in core.
predictions.Q7: The composed certificate is expressible as a bound the PARENT codec states from its own extent plus its auxiliaries' certificates, with no knowledge of what the auxiliary's codec is. FALSIFIED if composition needs the parent to know the auxiliary's FORMAT rather than its certificate — which would mean fidelity does not compose across the plugin boundary, and would be the most important thing this wave could find.
predictions.Q8: The retained-codebook profile can be priced without ever being selectable: the ledger takes a declared profile, and candidate enumeration is a separate surface. FALSIFIED if pricing a profile requires it to exist as a candidate — which would mean the accounting cannot describe a realization the executor does not have, and every 'what would it cost' question would have to be answered by building it.

not_claimed: No timing, no throughput, no kernel, and no compression claim: `VQ8_SHARED` is a forcing test for the dependency axis, not a quantiser anyone should use. Nothing here says a codebook is a good idea for any real model; it says the contract can carry one — and that carrying one does not make every auxiliary permanently resident or touched during execution.
exit_claim: A codec may depend on other represented objects without disguising them as byte streams: the dependency is resolved, validated, ordered, admitted before I/O, accounted by the SELECTED REALIZATION rather than by its role, composed into the parent's fidelity in a named norm over a named domain or refused, invalidated with its provider, and executed through the canonical path — with no part of the machinery knowing what a codebook is, and nothing pinnable that cannot be executed.
